source_review.notes: Checked twelve primary sources: the original Google MapReduce publication; current Apache Hadoop MapReduce tutorial/default configuration; current Apache Spark RDD, shuffle configuration, tuning, and monitoring documentation; current Apache Flink TaskManager memory, batch memory tuning, and configuration documentation; and current Dask worker-memory and shuffle documentation. All twelve URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date. Sources support serialized/accounting buffers, thresholds, spill/merge behavior, managed and process memory, shuffle configuration, metrics, and temporary-storage claims.

evidence: Reviewed nominal memory C, trigger fraction alpha, effective payload H, serialized bytes D, spill runs S, fan-in F, passes P, total I/O I, amplification A, and generation/service rates g and w.
Checked buffer, index, record, sort, codec, writer, frozen, heap, off-heap, native/direct, process, disk, and cache quantities remain distinct.
Checked attempt, exchange, spill generation, run, data/index, candidate, winner, and final-publication identities are used consistently.
notation_and_syntax.notes: All model quantities declare units and scope; engine counters and operating-system memory observations are explicitly not assumed equivalent.

evidence: Executed spill-merge-amplification with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced a 192.0 MiB target, 11 initial runs, fan-in four, and two passes.
Recomputed 4,096 MiB merge reads, 6,144 MiB total writes including initial spill, and 5.0-times full-rewrite I/O for 2,048 MiB serialized input.
Recomputed Exercise 1 as 20 runs, two passes, 12,000 MiB reads, 18,000 MiB total writes, 30,000 MiB total I/O, and five-times amplification.
Checked 97 runs at fan-in ten need two balanced passes.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The executable fixture validates a deterministic full-byte-pass model only and does not simulate variable records, concurrency, filesystems, codecs, or failures.

evidence: Verified H=alpha C, S=ceil(D/H), P=ceil(log_F S) for S>1 and F at least two.
Counted one initial write plus one read and write for each full merge pass to derive I=(1+2P)D and A=1+2P.
Reviewed backlog growth as the integral of generation minus service rate until bounded backpressure applies.
Checked combiner safety depends on closure/associativity and, under arbitrary order, commutativity plus numeric and side-effect semantics.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The I/O derivation is explicitly conditional on constant full-byte passes and changes with combining, compression, reuse, partial passes, caching, and retry.

evidence: Reviewed empty and single-run output, threshold/hard-limit equality, exact boundary collisions, giant records, metadata-dominant tiny records, fragmented capacity, and codec expansion.
Reviewed synchronous/asynchronous spill, both buffers occupied, writer starvation, generation rate exceeding service rate, lock/credit deadlock, and simultaneous worker spill.
Reviewed disk-full/slow/corrupt/removed devices, partial writes, missing runs, constrained descriptors/direct memory, cancellation, stale callbacks, process death, retry, and speculation.
Reviewed unsafe/nonreducing combiners, numeric/order effects, skewed producer run counts, memory-estimate/RSS disagreement, sensitive plaintext, and cleanup holds.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Memory safety, progress, artifact correctness, semantic aggregation, and lifecycle are treated as separate obligations.

evidence: Traced every accepted record through pinned destination, serialized bytes/index, frozen snapshot, immutable run, merge, final data/index, accepted attempt, and exchange publication.
Checked complete scalable memory charging, reserve below hard limit, bounded active/frozen buffers, giant-record handling, and backpressure.
Checked data/index range and format agreement, run immutability, merge destination/multiplicity/order preservation, and checksum validation.
Checked attempt-scoped namespaces, winner fencing, failure/cancellation states, safe memory release, idempotent cleanup, and security isolation.
invariant_checking.notes: Final output authority follows validated winner publication; completed spill runs remain private intermediate candidates.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from identity and complete memory charging through triggers, ownership, combiner algebra, runs, merge, correctness, measurement, fault injection, and governance.
Checked conditional boundedness requires every scalable allocation charged, bounded concurrent buffers, bounded oversize behavior, and backpressure before the hard ceiling.
Checked spill/merge correctness inductively from immutable partitioned snapshots through runs and every merge pass.

Reviewed counterexamples for nominal-buffer process bounds, full-capacity triggers, unlimited asynchronous overlap, arbitrary combining, per-destination files, compression assumptions, task visibility, immediate disk retry, and unconditional cleanup.
proof_review.notes: The proofs distinguish algorithm-owned bounds from hidden user/native memory and logical preservation from durability and accepted-attempt publication.

evidence: Audited uses of bounded, safe, complete, immutable, durable, exact, accepted, associative, atomic, amplification, and lower/soft/hard limits.
Confirmed the spill/pass/I/O equations are labeled simplified full-rewrite estimates and not runtime predictions or universal counters.
Confirmed managed memory, asynchronous spill, compression, combining, and larger buffers are not labeled universally sufficient or faster.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Implementation-specific thresholds and current product behavior are sourced and kept separate from the general state-machine model.

evidence: Reviewed proposed heap/off-heap/native/RSS, trigger, wait, spill, run, byte, ratio, time, per-device, retry, abandoned-work, and cleanup measurements.
Confirmed no universal memory size, threshold fraction, hysteresis, buffer count, run size, fan-in, codec, record limit, disk layout, or retention period is prescribed.
Checked logical/serialized/compressed/read/written/cached measures and mean/quantile/maximum distributions remain explicit.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production tuning requires workload records/keys, serializer/codec, task concurrency, memory allocator, device, failure, recovery, and policy evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed map-side buffering and spill as one bounded external-memory protocol spanning full memory accounting, buffer organization, thresholds, asynchronous ownership, sorting, combining, giant records, run/index format, external merge, disks, backpressure, attempts, observability, validation, and lifecycle.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed practical charge models, reserve and hysteresis, double-buffer limits, immutable run state machines, disk-full handling, merge fan-in, device contention, attempt namespaces, metric semantics, fault injection, tenant isolation, and deletion. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from memory inventory and triggering through spill mechanics, algebra, merge cost, failure, measurement, and governance. Ten examples and five complete answers cover accounting, boundaries, asynchronous flow, combiners, passes, giant records, disks, speculation, skew, and review design.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Spark, Flink, Hadoop, or Dask maintainer, runtime/memory-management researcher, external-sorting specialist, storage/performance engineer, security/privacy/legal/records authority, affected-tenant reviewer, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
